newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr impossible for farmers -- AFFCO's Jackson.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr impossible for farmers -- AFFCO's Jackson.

text.p: AFFCO Holdings Ltd Chairman Peter Jackson told the annual meeting on Thursday the strength of the New Zealand dollar was making business impossible for farmers.
Jackson told the annual meeting the exchange rate had wiped more than NZ$1 billion off returns to sheep and beef farmers in the last two years.
A 320 kg bull sold in the U.S. from December 1993 to December 1996 had lost NZ$227 in exchange rate movement and $296 in price movement.
"Farmers and other exporters are paying a very high price for the Reserve Bank's use of monetary policy to control inflation," Jackson said.

"I accept that a movement in the exchange rate close to the inflation rate of one or two percent is not difficult to sustain as an exporter, but when a farmer is asked to adjust to an exchange rate appreciation of 25-30 percent over two years, it is just not possible to re-adjust his business," he said.
Wool prices were heavily affected by the exchange rate and the the Kiwi's appreciation had a dramatic effect on the profitability of hill country farming, he said.
